overall: Atlanta has reached a running maximum of 82.4°F by 13:20 ET and continues to warm at +1.8°F/hr, with the intraday model placing the peak near 14:36 ET. The morning was significantly suppressed by persistent overcast (OVC from ~05:00–10:52 ET), which delayed meaningful heating until late morning; skies have since broken to BKN at 62% coverage with a relatively low ceiling of 853m, which is moderating but not blocking afternoon solar input. Active severe weather alerts are confined to South Georgia and North Florida — not a direct threat to Atlanta today.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models disagree by about 2.4°F: HRRR is most conservative at 83.8°F, ECMWF at 85.5°F, and NBM highest at 86.2°F, averaging near 85°F — all tracking below the NWS official narrative high of 88°F, which appears to have been set before the extended morning overcast and broken afternoon cloud deck became clear. The intraday model strongly favors the 86–87°F bucket (37.5%), while the META fused model splits evenly between 84–85°F and 86–87°F (both at 27.6%), with meaningful probability extending through 90°F.
max_temp_prediction: With 82.4°F already locked in as the running max at 13:20 ET and a positive warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, there is still upside potential of 3–5°F before the peak, but the low 853m ceiling, 62% broken cloud cover, and conservative NWP model consensus all suggest the NWS 88°F target is ambitious. The bulk of the probability mass in both the INTRADAY and META models sits in the 84–87°F range, making a final TMAX near 85.5°F the most defensible estimate; confidence is moderate given the cloud uncertainty and the ~2–4 hours of warming window still remaining.
